precision_note: Justified differently in different traditions: removal of original sin (Catholic) or the covenant sign (Reformed).
attack_1: One requires a personal profession the infant cannot give; the other treats baptism as a gift preceding response.
attack_2: The New Testament records only believers being baptised, and an infant cannot repent or profess faith.
defence_2: Household baptisms in Acts imply children were included, and grace precedes response.

name: Transubstantiation
definition: The Catholic doctrine that the substance of the elements becomes Christ's body and blood.
precision_note: Substance changes, appearances do not. The Aristotelian framework is what Protestants reject.
attack_1: One holds the elements changed, the other holds them unchanged signs of remembrance.

name: Real presence
definition: The belief that Christ is genuinely present in the eucharist.
precision_note: A family of views, not one: transubstantiation, sacramental union and spiritual presence all count.

name: Memorialism
definition: The view that communion is a remembrance with no change in the elements.
precision_note: The Baptist position the spec contrasts with the Catholic one.
attack_1: One holds the elements changed, the other holds them unchanged signs of remembrance.

name: Mission of the Church
definition: The Church's sending into the world.
precision_note: The spec asks specifically about developments from the early twentieth century to today, so track the shift from conversion to social action.
attack_1: Declining religious authority undercuts the Church's standing to pronounce on wealth and social order.

name: Militant atheism
definition: The active claim that religion is irrational and harmful.
precision_note: The spec names it as part of the challenge of secularisation, with McGrath as the reply.

name: Fresh Expressions
definition: New forms of church developed outside traditional parish structures.
precision_note: Named in the spec as a response to secularisation.

name: House Church movement
definition: Independent congregations meeting outside institutional church buildings.
precision_note: Named in the spec alongside Fresh Expressions.

name: Preferential option for the poor
definition: The claim that God sides with the oppressed and that theology must begin there.
precision_note: The core of liberation theology, which the spec names under social relevance.
attack_1: Liberation theology begins from the experience of the oppressed rather than from a fixed rational order.
attack_2: Liberation theology prioritises the poor as a matter of justice, not because it maximises aggregate welfare.

name: God of the gaps
definition: Invoking God to explain what science has not yet explained.
precision_note: A criticism of theism, not a version of it. Every gap that closes shrinks this God.

name: Creationism
definition: The literal reading of Genesis as an account of origins.
precision_note: Named in the spec among contemporary responses to the Big Bang. A minority Christian position, not the default.

name: Theistic evolution
definition: The view that evolution is the means by which God creates.
precision_note: The mainstream Catholic and Anglican position, and the reason science versus religion is a false binary here.

name: Big Bang cosmology
definition: The scientific account of the universe's origin from an initial expansion.
precision_note: Named in the spec. Arguably supports rather than threatens the cosmological argument, since it implies a beginning.

name: Reductionism
definition: Explaining religion wholly in terms of a lower-level process, psychological or neurological.
precision_note: The shared form of Freud's and Persinger's arguments; the shared reply is that origin does not settle truth.
attack_1: Swinburne's default trust and the reductionist default suspicion cannot both govern the same reports.
attack_2: Continuing charismatic gifts are claimed as present-day evidence against a purely natural account.

name: Roman Catholic
definition: Scripture and Tradition together, interpreted by the Magisterium; seven sacraments; transubstantiation; salvation through grace received in the sacraments.
precision_note: Named in the spec as the contrast to Protestant on the relative authority of Bible and Church, and to Baptist on baptism and Holy Communion.
notes: Origin: Continuous from the early Church; defined against the Reformation at Trent, 1545-63. Governance: Episcopal, under the Pope and Magisterium. Positions — Authority of Bible and Church: Co-equal; Infant baptism: Permits and requires; Holy Communion: Transubstantiation; Justification: By faith working through love; Predestination: Rejects the Calvinist form; Ordination of women: Forbids; Truth claims of other religions: Inclusivism; Evolution: Accepts; Genetic engineering: Conditional; Miracles: Affirms, with investigation; Abortion: Forbids; Voluntary euthanasia: Forbids; Capital punishment: Forbids; War: Conditional; just war; Animals: Stewardship with human priority; Same sex relationships: Forbids sexual acts.

name: Eastern Orthodox
definition: Scripture read within Holy Tradition; theosis as the goal of salvation; icons; the real presence affirmed without defining the mechanism.
precision_note: Useful third position: neither sola scriptura nor papal Magisterium, which complicates a simple Protestant-Catholic binary.
notes: Origin: Continuous from the early Church; separated from Rome at the Great Schism, 1054. Governance: Conciliar, autocephalous churches under patriarchs. Positions — Authority of Bible and Church: Scripture within Tradition; Infant baptism: Permits and requires; Holy Communion: Real presence, mechanism undefined; Predestination: Rejects; synergy; Ordination of women: Forbids; Truth claims of other religions: Exclusivist leaning.

name: Anglican
definition: Scripture supreme, with tradition and reason as supporting authorities; deliberately broad, holding Anglo-Catholic and Evangelical wings together.
precision_note: The spec names the debate about female ordination in the Church of England up to and after 1994 and its continuation today.
notes: Origin: English Reformation, 1534 onwards; the Elizabethan Settlement of 1559. Governance: Episcopal, with General Synod. Positions — Authority of Bible and Church: Scripture supreme, tradition and reason supporting; Infant baptism: Permits; Holy Communion: Range of views; Ordination of women: Permits; Evolution: Accepts; Abortion: Conditional; Same sex relationships: Contested.

name: Baptist
definition: Scripture alone as sole authority; believer's baptism by full immersion, rejecting infant baptism; Holy Communion as a memorial.
precision_note: Named in the spec as the contrast to the Catholic tradition on both baptism and Holy Communion.
notes: Origin: English separatism, from 1609. Governance: Congregational; each local church self-governing. Positions — Authority of Bible and Church: Scripture alone; Infant baptism: Forbids; Holy Communion: Memorial; Justification: By faith alone; Ordination of women: Varies by congregation.

name: Reformed
definition: Scripture alone; total depravity and predestination; justification by faith alone; a spiritual rather than physical presence in communion.
precision_note: The source of the predestination material the spec requires under good conduct, and of Calvin's total depravity.
notes: Origin: Calvin's Geneva, from 1541. Governance: Presbyterian, governed by elders in courts. Positions — Authority of Bible and Church: Scripture alone; Infant baptism: Permits; Holy Communion: Spiritual presence; Justification: By faith alone; Predestination: Affirms unconditional election; Miracles: Cessationist.

name: Lutheran
definition: Justification by faith alone as the central doctrine; Scripture alone; infant baptism retained; the real presence in, with and under the bread and wine.
precision_note: The clearest exponent of justification by faith, which the spec names alongside justification by works.
notes: Origin: Luther's reform, from 1517. Governance: Varies: episcopal in Scandinavia, synodical elsewhere. Positions — Infant baptism: Permits; Holy Communion: Sacramental union; Justification: By faith alone; Ordination of women: Permits in most churches.

name: Methodist
definition: Scripture, tradition, reason and experience together; Arminian rather than Calvinist, so prevenient grace is offered to all; strong social conscience.
precision_note: The Arminian counterweight to predestination, and an early example of the social relevance emphasis.
notes: Origin: Wesley's revival within Anglicanism, from 1738; separate from 1795. Governance: Connexional, with conference and circuits. Positions — Predestination: Rejects; Arminian; Ordination of women: Permits.

name: Pentecostal
definition: Baptism in the Holy Spirit with speaking in tongues; healing and prophecy as continuing gifts; believer's baptism; experiential rather than creedal emphasis.
precision_note: The strongest contemporary case for continuing miracles, which bears directly on the Hume and Wiles debate.
notes: Origin: Azusa Street revival, Los Angeles, 1906. Governance: Varies; often congregational with charismatic leadership. Positions — Infant baptism: Forbids; Miracles: Affirms as continuing.
attack_1: Continuing charismatic gifts are claimed as present-day evidence against a purely natural account.

name: Quaker
definition: The inner light in every person; no creed, no sacraments, no clergy; silent unprogrammed worship; historic pacifism.
precision_note: The limiting case on expressions of religious identity: a Christian tradition with neither baptism nor Holy Communion.
notes: Origin: George Fox and the English radical reformation, from 1652. Governance: Meeting-based, with no ordained ministry. Positions — Infant baptism: Rejects the practice entirely; Holy Communion: Rejects the practice entirely; Ordination of women: Not applicable; no ordained ministry; Abortion: Conditional; War: Forbids; pacifism; Same sex relationships: Permits; Wealth and possessions: Simplicity.

name: Liberal Christianity
definition: Non-propositional revelation; the Bible as inspired but humanly written; miracle and resurrection often read symbolically; demythologisation.
precision_note: The spec requires the impact of nineteenth-century biblical criticism and the resulting freedom to challenge traditional readings.
notes: Origin: Nineteenth-century biblical criticism and the encounter with modern science. Governance: Not a denomination; a tendency within many. Positions — Authority of Bible and Church: Scripture as humanly written witness; Truth claims of other religions: Pluralist leaning; Evolution: Accepts; Genetic engineering: Conditional; Miracles: Anti-realist; Abortion: Conditional; Animals: Stewardship; Same sex relationships: Permits.

name: Evangelical conservatism
definition: Biblical inerrancy; propositional revelation; literal reading of Genesis and of the resurrection; creationism or intelligent design.
precision_note: Supplies the creationist responses to Darwin and the Big Bang that the spec names under Christianity and science.
notes: Origin: American fundamentalist movement, from about 1910. Governance: Not a denomination; a tendency within many. Positions — Authority of Bible and Church: Scripture inerrant; Ordination of women: Forbids; Truth claims of other religions: Exclusivism; Evolution: Rejects; Capital punishment: Permits; Animals: Dominion; Wealth and possessions: Personal stewardship.

name: Liberation theology
definition: God's preferential option for the poor; theology begins from praxis and from the experience of the oppressed; structural sin.
precision_note: Named in the spec as the emphasis on the social relevance of Christianity in support of oppressed people and those in poverty.
notes: Origin: Latin America, from the 1960s; Gutierrez, 1971. Governance: Base communities alongside existing structures. Positions — Wealth and possessions: Structural critique.

name: Wealth and possessions
definition: The moral status of property, accumulation and generosity in Christian teaching.
precision_note: Named in the spec under responses to materialistic secular values. Every ethical theory takes a position on it, which is why it is a common Section C cell.
interacts_with: Preferential option for the poor; Liberation theology

name: Theft
definition: Taking what belongs to another without consent.
precision_note: The spec names theft and lying as the two issues the three normative theories must be applied to. Do not skip them: they are the illustration examiners ask for by name.
interacts_with: Lying; Natural moral law; Situation ethics

name: Lying
definition: Deliberately asserting what one believes to be false.
precision_note: Kant's murderer-at-the-door case lives here, and the spec also uses lying under conscience. It bridges ET01, ET06 and ET10.
spec_codes: ET01; ET02; ET03; ET04; ET06; ET10

name: Breaking promises
definition: Failing to keep an undertaking freely given.
precision_note: Named in the spec under the role of conscience, alongside telling lies. Kant's universalisability test handles it cleanly.

name: Adultery
definition: Sexual relations by a married person with someone other than their spouse.
precision_note: Named in the spec as a conscience issue, not an applied-ethics issue. Approach it through what conscience says, not through the theories.

name: Marriage
definition: The union of two people, understood in Christianity as covenantal and, traditionally, lifelong.
precision_note: Named in the Section C dialogue list. Catholic teaching treats it as a sacrament; most Protestant traditions do not.
interacts_with: Same sex relationships; Adultery; Natural moral law

name: Same sex relationships
definition: Sexual and romantic relationships between people of the same sex.
precision_note: Named in both Section A and the Section C dialogue list. The dispute is whether the biblical prohibitions are culturally conditioned.
interacts_with: Marriage; Natural moral law; Situation ethics
attack_1: The spec's own contrast: a theory ordered to natural ends and a lived reality it excludes.

name: Transgender matters
definition: Questions about gender identity and its recognition within Christian teaching and practice.
precision_note: Named in the spec alongside marriage and same sex relationships. Traditions divide on whether created sex is theologically fixed.

name: Genetic engineering
definition: Deliberate modification of an organism's genetic material.
precision_note: Named in the spec twice: under Christianity and science, and in the Section C dialogue list. Distinguish somatic from germline editing.
interacts_with: Designer babies; Cloning; Sanctity of life

name: Tolerance
definition: Accepting the presence and practice of beliefs one holds to be mistaken.
precision_note: Named in the Section C dialogue list beside wealth and freedom of religious expression. Exclusivism and pluralism give different accounts of what tolerance requires.
interacts_with: Freedom of religious expression; Religious pluralism

name: Freedom of religious expression
definition: The right to hold and practise a religion publicly.
precision_note: The spec ties it to European law and to religious pluralism as a feature of modern secular states.
attack_1: Relegating religion to the personal sphere restricts the public expression the right is meant to protect.

name: Resurrection of the flesh
definition: Augustine's teaching that the same body is raised, transformed but continuous with the one that died.
precision_note: The spec names Augustine here specifically. Distinguish it from spiritual resurrection, which the spec also lists.
presented_by: Augustine of Hippo (Bishop of Hippo Regius, 354–430) — "resurrection of the flesh"
attack_1: Paul says flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom, so a literal raising of the same matter is not what is promised.
defence_1: Augustine argues transformation preserves identity, since it is this body glorified rather than another.
defender_1: Augustine of Hippo (Bishop of Hippo Regius, 354–430) — "resurrection of the flesh"

name: Spiritual resurrection
definition: The view that what is raised is a spiritual body rather than the physical flesh.
precision_note: Rests on 1 Corinthians 15:42-44, sown a natural body and raised a spiritual body. The liberal alternative to Augustine.
interacts_with: Resurrection of the flesh; Objective immortality

name: The soul
definition: The Christian concept of the self that God creates, judges and raises.
precision_note: Christian usage is not Platonic: the soul is created rather than pre-existent, and needs the body to be complete.
attack_1: If mental life is brain activity, there is no soul to be judged or raised.
defence_1: Christian hope rests on God raising the person, not on an immortal soul surviving independently.
